initial.prompt: Create one premium Kalistar narrative PAINTING, portrait 4:5, illustration only. FORTUNE (Helena Dolph Jackson) from METAL GEAR SOLID 2, her FIRST CONFRONTATION with Raiden INSIDE the Big Shell Strut A Deep Sea Dock industrial hangar. Faithfully recognizable adult BLACK woman with warm medium-dark brown skin, athletic tall build, distinctive shoulder-length golden BLONDE hair swept back in loose waves, a few falling locks, strong cheekbones, natural human face proportions. Mature expressive face: weary grief and simmering anger, lips slightly parted as though challenging her unseen opponent, steady searching eyes, not grinning, not posing seductively. Accurate MGS2 outfit: fitted dark navy/black high-neck short-sleeved tactical bodysuit with brief-cut lower portion, bare thighs, olive tactical harness and broad utility belt with rectangular pouches, one strapped thigh holster, fingerless dark gloves, sturdy black mid-calf military boots, dark short shoulder cape with divided cloth tails behind. Practical worn fabric, not lingerie or glossy latex. Pose: she deliberately steps forward on the hangar floor, weight solid and natural, facing camera in a slight three-quarter turn. Both hands physically carry her HUGE signature portable electromagnetic RAILGUN across her lower torso, visibly heavy. This is NOT a sniper rifle, assault rifle, minigun, bazooka or tiny gun. Correct silhouette verified from the game's first-boss cinematic: massive angular olive/black box-shaped rear receiver, raised carry handle with compact box optic on top, TWO very long STRAIGHT PARALLEL rectangular rails forming an open slotted barrel, a squared forked/open muzzle, one rear trigger grip and forward support grip, coherent solid assembly without bent barrel or extra handles. Gun total length around 1.3-1.5 metres compared to the woman, far larger than a normal rifle; keep its main shape and front muzzle clearly readable. Aim diagonally DOWN toward viewer-right so the long rails run from her centre-left waist toward x72%,y74%, mostly side-on with mild foreshortening. Both grips connect correctly to the weapon and natural hands. A small restrained blue-white electric arc bridges the muzzle rails, not a giant glowing beam. Head around x48%,y22%; character from head to boots spans about 75% image height. Essential face, hands, weapon and muzzle within central x22%-78% band because card stat columns will cover edges. Leave background breathing room and floor below her boots. Scene: an ENCLOSED utilitarian maritime cargo hangar/deep sea dock, olive steel and ochre-painted wall panels, industrial elevator door behind, a few stacked dark green metal transport crates to the sides, overhead fluorescent strips and pipes, slightly damp concrete/steel floor with soft reflections. Coherent realistic architecture, sparse industrial background, not an outdoor oil rig, cathedral, generic spaceship or flooded pool. Cinematic but readable: pale industrial light across her brown skin and blonde hair, subtle warmer practical side light and cool railgun accent. KALISTAR GOLDEN RULE: detailed narrative fantasy oil/digital PAINTING in the same family as the viewed approved Momo and Valazar illustrations, purposeful visible brushstrokes, broken painted edges, sculpted color planes on face and hands, tactile worn textiles and chipped metal, subdued background detail, emotional individuality. Natural anatomy but unmistakably PAINTED, NOT photographic, NOT smooth 3D, NOT anime/manga, NOT cel-shaded. One head, two arms, two hands, two legs; no anatomy obscured by decorative magic. No text, logos, numbers, UI, card frame, border or watermark.

selected.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Edit target Image 1: the Fortune illustration. Supporting STYLE references Images 2 and 3: approved Kalistar Momo and Valazar. Repaint Image 1 as a complete cohesive artwork in the SAME PAINTED LANGUAGE as Images 2 and 3, not a texture filter. Preserve the recognizable adult Black blonde woman Fortune from Metal Gear Solid 2, her first encounter inside Big Shell's enclosed cargo/deep-sea-dock hangar, her grieving defiant expression, dark short-sleeved high-neck tactical bodysuit, olive harness and utility pouches, bare thighs, gloves, black military boots, short dark shoulder cape, her heavy enormous twin-rail electromagnetic gun carried with both hands. Keep weapon mechanically straight and coherent with two long parallel rectangular barrel rails, bulky box receiver and compact top optic. Preserve brown skin and blonde wavy hair. PRIMARY CORRECTION: the face and limbs must be visibly PAINTED with confident interlocking warm and cool COLOR PLANES, selected sharp edges around eyes and hands, lost edges in shadow, broad broken bristle strokes describing form, as in Momo/Valazar; eliminate photographic skin rendering, individual pore detail and smooth 3D-like gradient modeling. Show expressive eyes, weary anger and humanity, not a neutral fashion pose. Paint fabric and metal using purposeful irregular strokes and larger planes, not repetitive fine scratches everywhere. Keep scene readable and understated: dark olive steel hangar, a few crates, overhead fluorescent strips, floor reflections reduced to broad painterly shapes. Prioritize face, hands and gun through lighting and selective detail; soften background edges. Motivated cool overhead light plus restrained warmer reflected light, a tiny blue-white arc between the gun's muzzle rails. No excessive electric effects. Composition for Kalistar's central card window: vertical 4:5, woman and weapon central with breathing room above head and below boots. Shift the muzzle composition slightly inward and lower, keeping the full long straight gun through a credible downward angle and perspective, not shortening or bending it; important muzzle should sit inside x80% rather than at the image edge. Two hands correctly attached to grips. This is fantasy narrative painted realism with natural anatomy, NOT photorealism, NOT anime/manga, NOT flat cel shading, NOT a uniform mosaic/noise filter. No Momo robot, no Valazar skeleton, no borrowing their costume or scenery. No text, logo, frame, card stats or watermark. Final illustration should look naturally part of the same collection as references 2 and 3.
